extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent prosecutors, patent attorneys, and patent agents (practitioners evaluating patentability under the AIA)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining patent applications under the America Invents Act (AIA) changes to 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103, including definitions, prior art categories, exceptions (grace period, derivation/common ownership), effective filing date rules, and applicability/transition rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) prior art categories
rubrics_metrics.description: A person is not entitled to a patent if the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the categories of disclosure treated as prior art under 102(a)(1). Under the AIA these public activities need not be in the United States (no geographic requirement). See MPEP § 2152.02 for detailed subtopics (patented, printed publication, public use, on sale, otherwise available).

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) prior art (U.S. patent documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person is not entitled to a patent if the claimed invention was described in a patent issued under 35 U.S.C. 151, or in an application for patent published or deemed published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b), that names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, and WIPO (PCT) publications that designate the U.S. (treated as applications deemed published under 122(b)). The reference is prior art only to the subject matter it describes and is effective as of its 'effectively filed' date under 35 U.S.C. 102(d). See MPEP § 2154.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions in 35 U.S.C. 100: 'claimed invention' (100(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'claimed invention' is defined as the subject matter defined by a claim in a patent or an application for a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify the subject matter to which effective filing date and prior art rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'effective filing date' (35 U.S.C. 100(i)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a claimed invention in a patent or application (other than a reissue or reissued patent), the effective filing date is the earlier of: (1) the actual filing date of the patent or application containing the claimed invention; or (2) the filing date of the earliest provisional, nonprovisional, international (PCT), or foreign patent application to which the patent or application is entitled to benefit or priority as to such claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effective filing date controls whether a disclosure is before or after the claimed invention for prior art purposes. The earlier application must support the claimed invention as required by 35 U.S.C. 112(a). See MPEP § 2152.01 and § 2153.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'inventor' and 'joint inventor' (35 U.S.C. 100(f) and 100(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'inventor' is the individual (or individuals collectively, for a joint invention) who invented or discovered the subject matter of the invention. 'Joint inventor'/'coinventor' means any one of the individuals who invented or discovered the subject matter of a joint invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant to identifying whose disclosures and actions can trigger or be excepted from prior art (e.g., inventor-originated disclosures under 102(b)(1)/(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1) inventor-originated disclosure exception (one-year grace period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain disclosures made one year or less before the effective filing date shall not be prior art under 102(a)(1) if: (1) the disclosure was made by the inventor or joint inventor or by another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor/joint inventor; or (2) the subject matter disclosed had, before such disclosure, been publicly disclosed by the inventor/joint inventor or by another who obtained it directly or indirectly from the inventor/joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This effectively provides a one-year grace period for an inventor-originated disclosure; the grace period is measured from the filing date of the earliest U.S. or foreign patent application to which benefit or priority is properly asserted and which supports the claimed invention under 35 U.S.C. 112(a). The grace period is extended to the next business day if it ends on a weekend or federal holiday (35 U.S.C. 21(b)). See MPEP § 2153 and subsections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may benefit from the 102(b)(1) grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor, joint inventor, assignee, obligated assignee, or other party having sufficient interest may file a patent application within the one-year grace period and avoid certain inventor-originated disclosures being prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grace-period entitlement is measured relative to the effective filing date and the earliest application to which priority/benefit is claimed that supports the claimed invention (112(a) support). See MPEP § 2153 and §§ 2153.01(a), 2153.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of the AIA grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: The one-year grace period in AIA 102(b)(1) is measured from the filing date of the earliest U.S. or foreign patent application to which a proper benefit or priority claim is asserted and the earlier application supports the claimed invention as required by 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differs from pre-AIA 102(b) (which measured from the filing date of the earliest U.S. application). Regulations governing filing dates (e.g., Priority Mail Express deposit, electronic filing) do not alter this statutory measurement; see MPEP §§ 2153.01(a) and 2153.02 for interactions with 37 C.F.R. filing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(A) and (B) exceptions to 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure shall not be prior art under 102(a)(2) if: (A) the subject matter disclosed was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor; or (B) the subject matter disclosed had, before such subject matter was effectively filed under 102(a)(2), been publicly disclosed by the inventor or joint inventor or another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exceptions mirror the inventor-originated protection for U.S. patent-document prior art; see MPEP § 2154.02(a)-(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) common ownership/assignment exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure in a U.S. patent document shall not be prior art under 102(a)(2) if, not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention, the disclosed subject matter and the claimed invention were owned by the same person or were subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the pre-AIA 103(c) limited rule and applies only to 102(a)(2) prior art (U.S. patent documents that were effectively filed earlier). It does not remove disclosures that are prior art under 102(a)(1) (patents, printed publications, public uses, sales, or other public disclosures). See MPEP § 2154.02(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) 'effectively filed' for 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. patent document is considered to have been effectively filed for prior art effect under 102(a)(2) as of the earlier of: (1) the actual filing date of the patent or application; or (2) if entitled to claim the benefit of or priority to an earlier application (U.S. provisional/nonprovisional, PCT, or foreign application), the filing date of the earliest such application that describes the subject matter of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus a U.S. patent document's prior art date is the filing date of the earliest application to which benefit is claimed and which describes the relied-upon subject matter, regardless of whether that earlier application was provisional, international, or foreign. See MPEP § 2154.01(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of WIPO (PCT) published applications as U.S. patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the AIA, a WIPO publication of a PCT international application that designates the United States is an application for patent deemed published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) for purposes of 102(a)(2), and thus is prior art if effectively filed earlier than the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is true regardless of the international filing date, whether published in English, or whether the PCT application later enters the U.S. national stage. Pre-AIA rules were more restrictive (e.g., PCT publication treated as a U.S. publication only under certain conditions). See MPEP § 2154.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic requirement removed for prior public use/on sale under AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pre-AIA 102, knowledge/use or public use/sale required the activity to be in the United States to qualify as prior art; under AIA 102(a)(1), prior public use, sale activity, or other disclosure has no geographic requirement and may be anywhere to qualify as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change expands the universe of potential 102(a)(1) prior art to foreign public activities and publications. See MPEP § 2152.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of invention no longer relevant under AIA 102
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of invention (i.e., proof of having invented prior to a prior art disclosure) is not relevant under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102; a prior art disclosure cannot be antedated merely by showing the inventor invented the claimed invention before the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antedating by showing earlier invention (e.g., via 37 C.F.R. 1.131) is not effective against AIA 102 prior art. This alters practices under pre-AIA 102 where date of invention could matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA elimination and limited carryover of certain pre-AIA 102 provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIA eliminates pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) (abandonment of the invention), 102(d) (premature foreign patenting), 102(f) (derivation), and 102(g) (prior invention by another), but pre-AIA 102(g) retains limited applicability in certain transition circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues such as an application that names a person who is not the actual inventor (pre-AIA 102(f) situations) are handled under derivation proceedings (35 U.S.C. 135), correction of inventorship (37 C.F.R. 1.48), or through rejections under 35 U.S.C. 101/115. See MPEP § 2157 and § 2159 for transition rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) deemed common ownership for joint research agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter disclosed and a claimed invention shall be deemed to have been owned by the same person (or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person) for purposes of applying the 102(b)(2)(C) exception if: (1) the subject matter disclosed was developed and the claimed invention was made by, or on behalf of, one or more parties to a joint research agreement that was in effect on or before the effective filing date; (2) the claimed invention was made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the joint research agreement; and (3) the application discloses or is amended to disclose the names of the parties to the joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'joint research agreement' is defined in 35 U.S.C. 100(h) as a written contract, grant, or cooperative agreement between two or more persons or entities for experimental, developmental, or research work in the field of the claimed invention. See MPEP § 2154 and § 2156.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 103 obviousness standard under AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may not be obtained if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to a person having ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AIA preserves the substantive obviousness inquiry of pre-AIA 103 but shifts the temporal focus to before the effective filing date (rather than time of invention) and states that patentability is not negated by the manner in which the invention was made. Pre-AIA 103(c) provisions were replaced by 102(b)(2)(C) (common ownership) and (c). See MPEP § 2158 and Chapter 2100 cross-references (2141 et seq.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability/Transition date for AIA 102 and 103
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 took effect on March 16, 2013. These provisions apply to any patent application that contains or contained at any time: (1) a claim to a claimed invention with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013; or (2) a designation as a continuation, divisional, or CIP of an application that ever contained a claim with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such applications are referred to as AIA (first-inventor-to-file) applications and the AIA rules apply to patents resulting from them. See Public Law 112-29 and MPEP § 2159 et seq. for transitional and mixed-claim scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued applicability of pre-AIA 102(g) in transition circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) apply to each claim of an AIA application if the application: (1) contains or contained at any time a claimed invention having an effective filing date before March 16, 2013; or (2) is ever designated as a continuation, divisional, or CIP of an application that contains or contained at any time a claim having an effective filing date before March 16, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-AIA 102(g) also applies to any patent resulting from an AIA application to which pre-AIA 102(g) applied. See MPEP § 2159 and § 2138 for guidance and form paragraphs (e.g., form paragraph 7.14.aia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitations of the 102(b)(2)(C) exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The 102(b)(2)(C) exception only removes disclosures as prior art under 102(a)(2) (U.S. patent documents effectively filed earlier) and does not except disclosures that are prior art under 102(a)(1) (patents, printed publications, public uses, sales, or other publicly available disclosures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, commonly-owned co-worker/collaborator disclosures that qualify as 102(a)(1) prior art are not excused merely by common ownership; they must fall within an applicable 102(b)(1) exception to be excused. See MPEP § 2154 and § 2152 discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical consequences for derivation and misnaming inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations where an application names a person who is not the actual inventor (pre-AIA 102(f) type scenarios) will be handled in a derivation proceeding under 35 U.S.C. 135, by correction of inventorship under 37 C.F.R. 1.48, or through a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 and 115.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and practitioners should follow MPEP § 2157 for procedures and applicable statutory/regulatory remedies rather than treating such issues as prior-art 102(f) problems.
